PilotResolutionGate: Positive ClearMs/WallMs, every interval exceeds timestamp-pair median, summed ticks >=2*8*max(1,timestamp-pair median). Invalid pilots are retained; no repeat and no candidate warm timing.
AllocationHandling: Preserve all nonnegative observed byte counts; report candidate-positive allocation differences as adverse and equal nonzero runtime overhead separately.
CacheScope: Methods warmed; sequential fixed128-container cohort, all refilled then cleared in order. No cache flushing; neither universal cache-cold nor repeatedly clearing one hot container.
ColdScope: First public Clear after identical normal registry/container setup in a fresh process. Observer/reflection/hash work excluded. Caller JIT can precede timestamp; process launch, native JIT allocation and universal runtime-cold behavior are not measured.
Scope: Runtime candidate and exact original baseline are unchanged from the wrapper screen.
One original-only pilot with both Clear-only and full-block wall durations; all count components persisted before candidate warm timing.
The1000ms estimated row budget is only a forecast; the fixed600s process-group deadline is authoritative.
Nine rows in four balanced process pairs. Eight cold fixtures each get three fresh-process samples per source/backend; cold order has two AB and one BA pair.
Short/capped/timer-dominated/GC-confounded data remain visible and cannot establish acceptance. Timestamp overhead is never subtracted.
Expected poststate hashes encode the Clear transformation; before and after are not expected to match. Owned arrays and capacities are verified outside timing.

Owned-array equality does not measure added helper native/JIT footprint. First-call samples are descriptive and can expose repeatable large adverse behavior; three samples cannot establish reliable cold-latency wins.
PublicEvidence: Only the explicit JSON allowlist. No actual paths, commands, environment dumps, compiler response files, target assemblies or private prior evidence.
